title: The Octopus That Has Three Hearts — and Loses One to Swim 😱
script: This sounds fake — but one sea creature shuts part of itself off just to move. The octopus runs three hearts simultaneously. Two pump blood to the gills. One pumps it to the body. The moment it swims, that third heart stops completely. That's why octopuses crawl instead of swim — swimming literally knocks out their main heart. But here's the strange part: their blood is blue, copper-based, and runs through all three hearts at once. Half of you won't believe a three-hearted animal voluntarily shuts one down to survive.
search_summary: Octopuses have three hearts and their systemic heart stops beating when they swim, making crawling more efficient.
comment_question: Would you rather have three hearts that fail mid-swim, or just one? 🐙
source_note: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, cephalopod biology literature
